entries.clue: LA Times first with leader on silly municipal regulations (6)

indicators.note: tells you the LA follows the word for 'times', which goes first
the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: 'times' as in multiplication: three by four
taken as printed
W is the standard abbreviation for with
its leader, the first letter

annotation.surface: A newspaper's front page leads on some foolish new city rules.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics dress the first two words as the Los Angeles newspaper; ignore them, because 'times' works as the multiplication word, as in three by four.
annotation.definitionFit: Bylaws are the regulations a local council makes for its own area.

entries.clue: Most of rear end and pecs area is maximally macho (8)

indicators.note: take most of the word, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: BUTT, a rear end, minus its last letter
the pecs are the chest muscles

annotation.surface: A gym-goer's backside and chest are as manly as they come.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is body-building, so 'maximally macho' reads as praise for the physique rather than a superlative adjective waiting to be built.
annotation.definitionFit: Butchest is the superlative of butch, so it means most macho.

entries.clue: We’re told of shelter in a field (3)

indicators.note: what we are told we hear, so the answer sounds like the word

blocks.note: a lee is a sheltered side, out of the wind

annotation.surface: Someone reports a hut standing in a meadow.
annotation.walkthrough: LEA is a poetic word for a meadow, and LEE (shelter, as in the lee of a wall) sounds just the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A lea is an open grassy field or meadow.

entries.clue: Kit swears wildly, has fun on a lake? (5-4)

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about wildly into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone called Kit curses furiously and then enjoys a day on the lake.
annotation.walkthrough: Kit reads as a person's name, but it is just three letters of fodder; the question mark marks the definition as one example of having fun on a lake.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who water-skis is towed across a lake for fun.

entries.clue: Father Ted’s Jewish counterpart went on? (8)

blocks.note: a Catholic priest's title, whose Jewish counterpart is needed
a rabbi is to a synagogue what a Father is to a parish
the name from the sitcom title, kept as printed, its possessive dropped

annotation.surface: A question about who would play the Irish priest of TV's Father Ted in a Jewish version.
annotation.walkthrough: Father Ted is a British sitcom about an Irish priest; swap the Catholic title for its Jewish equivalent and RABBI TED appears. To rabbit on is British slang for talk at length.
annotation.definitionFit: Rabbited means talked on and on, as in 'rabbited on about his holiday'.

entries.clue: Irrational, as the nastiest numbers? (13)

indicators.note: the letters stop making sense, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A maths quip about which numbers are the most irrational and nasty.
annotation.walkthrough: With 'Irrational' and 'numbers' together, the clue sounds like maths, but a numb-er here is something that numbs.
annotation.definitionFit: Anaesthetists numb patients before surgery, so they are literally numbers.

entries.clue: Modern experimental facility sent back curry (5)

indicators.note: what is sent back is returned, so read it right to left

blocks.note: an IT lab, a computer laboratory

annotation.surface: A trendy test kitchen returns a curry to the chef.
annotation.walkthrough: Sending food back in a restaurant is the surface; the curry in question is itself the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A balti is a curry cooked and served in a wok-like metal bowl, a Birmingham favourite.

entries.clue: Swap short amount of time – about time! – for confidential info (5,6)

indicators.note: a short amount of time is an abbreviated one

blocks.note: to swap is to trade
SEC, short for second
re = about, concerning
T is the standard abbreviation for time

annotation.surface: Someone impatiently offers a quick deal in exchange for inside information.
annotation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'about time!' look like an exclamation of impatience; it is really two pieces, RE and T.
annotation.definitionFit: A trade secret is information a business keeps confidential, like a recipe or process.

entries.clue: Most of words rejected; Everyman’s beginning to get tired (6)

definitions.note: 'to get tired' stands for the verb drowse, to become sleepy

indicators.note: take most of the word, dropping its last letter
what is rejected is turned back, so read it right to left
the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: WORDS minus its last letter
the possessive S kept as a letter
its beginning, the first letter

annotation.surface: The setter complains that his words keep being turned down and he is starting to flag.
annotation.walkthrough: The S is the awkward piece: it comes from the possessive in Everyman’s, placed before Everyman's first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To drowse is to grow sleepy, to be half asleep.

entries.clue: This restaurant’ll advertise tasty tapenades, olives, ricotta – Italian antipasti – you’ll want the starters! (9)

definitions.text: This restaurant’ll advertise tasty tapenades, olives, ricotta – Italian antipasti – you’ll want the starters!

indicators.note: the starters of words are their first letters

blocks.clueFragment: This restaurant’ll advertise tasty tapenades, olives, ricotta – Italian antipasti
blocks.note: first letters of the nine words

annotation.surface: A menu blurb for an Italian place boasting of its antipasti.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the description: 'the starters' is a restaurant word for first courses, and also for first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian restaurant, the sort that would serve these antipasti.

entries.clue: In sum, I might be one of these? (5,8)

definitions.text: In sum, I might be one of these?

blocks.note: the surface reads I as the speaker, taking part in a total; the setter means the letter I as it appears written in a sum
the surface wonders whether the speaker belongs to a group; the setter means the letter I stands for the number one

annotation.surface: A person wondering whether they count as one of a group.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I' reads as the speaker, but it is the letter I, which is the Roman numeral for one, in a sum.
annotation.definitionFit: Roman numerals are the letters I, V, X, L, C, D and M used as numbers, and I is one of them.

entries.clue: Plain and somewhat porcellanous (5)

indicators.note: only some of the word is used

blocks.note: porcel(LANO)us, hidden in the middle

annotation.surface: Describing a pale, porcelain-like face as plain.
annotation.walkthrough: Plain reads as an adjective, homely, but it is the noun: a grassy plain.
annotation.definitionFit: A llano is a wide grassy plain in Spanish America.

entries.clue: One rambling, greeting king and queen once (5)

blocks.note: hi, a greeting
K for king, as in chess
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

annotation.surface: A chatterbox who once met the king and queen and won't stop talking about it.
annotation.walkthrough: Rambling suggests talking on and on; here it means walking in the countryside.
annotation.definitionFit: Rambling is the British word for leisurely country walking, so a rambler is a plain synonym for this walker.

entries.clue: City playing United, twice – plural – a matey kickaround, at first (5,6)

indicators.note: the letters are at play, moving into a new order
take the first letters of the words before

blocks.note: U for United, as in football results, twice
the word kept as printed
kept as printed
first letters

annotation.surface: A football report: City take on United in a friendly kickabout.
annotation.walkthrough: City and United sound like two English football clubs; City is the definition and United only gives a U.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Malaysia's capital is one instance of a city.

entries.clue: Powerful scent: a billionaire’s characteristic? (9)

definitions.note: 'Powerful scent' describes the quality muskiness, a noun for the smell's character

blocks.note: the heavy animal smell of musk, used in perfumes
the quality of being like Elon Musk, the billionaire, with a noun-making suffix on his surname

annotation.surface: A perfume advert suggesting a strong scent is the mark of the super-rich.
annotation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a joke on Elon Musk, the billionaire: Musk-iness is being like Musk.
annotation.definitionFit: Muskiness is the heavy, powerful smell of musk.

entries.clue: Small Houyhnhnm, one hiding actual intentions? (8-5)

blocks.note: S for small, as on clothing labels
the Houyhnhnms are the talking horses of Gulliver's Travels

annotation.surface: A little horse from Swift's satire that keeps its real motives to itself.
annotation.walkthrough: The Houyhnhnms are the rational, speaking horses Gulliver meets in Jonathan Swift's book.
annotation.definitionFit: A stalking-horse is a person or thing used to conceal someone's real plans, originally a horse hunters hid behind.

entries.clue: No coal tar involved in type of surgery (4,5)

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up, involved with each other

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A reassurance that no coal tar is used in some operation.
annotation.walkthrough: Coal tar sounds like a medical ingredient, which keeps the surface in the surgery.
annotation.definitionFit: Root canal treatment is dental surgery on the pulp inside a tooth.

entries.clue: Green tea brewed for youngster (8)

indicators.note: brewing mixes the ingredients, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Making a cup of green tea for a young person.
annotation.walkthrough: Brewed fits the tea so snugly that it is easy to miss as an anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A teenager is a youngster aged thirteen to nineteen.

entries.clue: An entrée with cured cod announced where soldiers get fit? (7,6)

indicators.note: what is announced is spoken, so the answer sounds like the words

blocks.note: an entrée is a course, and cod that is cured is salt cod

annotation.surface: A waiter announces a starter of salt cod.
annotation.walkthrough: The dining-room surface hides an army training ground: say 'a salt course' quickly and it becomes ASSAULT COURSE.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the obstacle ground of walls, nets and ditches is exactly where army recruits build fitness.

entries.clue: Carry, with difficulty, a little kitsch leprechaun (6)

indicators.note: only a little of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

annotation.surface: Someone lugging a tacky garden-ornament leprechaun about.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after Carry makes 'with difficulty' part of the definition, not a separate instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: To schlep is to haul something heavy or awkward, from Yiddish.

entries.clue: Many like a society without aristocrats (9)

blocks.note: too numerous to be counted
a society lacking counts, the noble title, read as the title plus a suffix meaning without

annotation.surface: A remark that many people would like to live in a society with no nobility.
annotation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word: a society with no counts is count-less.
annotation.definitionFit: Countless means too many to count.

entries.clue: Kind of song that brings illumination (5)

definitions.note: 'Kind of song' is a noun phrase; TORCH works as the modifier in 'torch song'

blocks.note: a sentimental ballad of unrequited love
a hand-held light; in Britain, a flashlight

annotation.surface: A song that is enlightening.
annotation.walkthrough: A torch song is a sentimental ballad of unrequited love; in Britain a torch is also a flashlight.
annotation.definitionFit: A torch gives light, and a torch song is a lovelorn ballad.

entries.clue: Replace a partner’s copper vessel (3,2)

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a tin is a container

annotation.surface: Swapping out a colleague's copper pot.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s reads as a possessive but is a link (partner's = partner is); on the dance floor, to cut in is to take over someone's partner.
annotation.definitionFit: To cut in is to interrupt a dancing couple and take one partner's place.

entries.clue: Outcast’s check rejected (5)

indicators.note: what is rejected is turned back, so read it right to left

blocks.note: to check an attack is to repel it

annotation.surface: An outcast's cheque bounces.
annotation.walkthrough: Check reads as a bank cheque that bounces; it is the verb, to hold back.
annotation.definitionFit: A leper, figuratively, is someone shunned by others.

entries.clue: Exotic tanginess getting act of approval (9)

indicators.note: the letters are made strange, rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A food critic gives the thumbs-up to an unusual sharp flavour.
annotation.walkthrough: ASSENTING here is a noun, the act of agreeing, which is why the definition is 'act of approval' rather than a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A gerund used as a noun: the verb assent means agree, so its -ing form names the act of giving approval.

entries.clue: Sit fast, regularly dismissing uncertainties (3)

indicators.note: dismiss every other letter at regular intervals

blocks.note: s(I)t (F)a(S)t: keep the second, fourth and sixth letters

annotation.surface: Stand firm and brush aside all doubts.
annotation.walkthrough: Sit fast reads as an instruction to hold firm; it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Ifs, as in 'no ifs or buts', are doubts or uncertainties.

entries.clue: Procure leverage (8)

blocks.note: verb: obtain by buying
noun: a firm grip or foothold that lets you apply force

annotation.walkthrough: Leverage reads as a verb beside Procure, but it is the noun: getting a purchase on a lid means getting a grip on it.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are plain synonyms, one verb (buy) and one the older mechanical noun sense of a grip for applying force.

entries.clue: Nearer the end (6)

blocks.note: comparative of close, said with a hard S
something that closes, like the last song of a show, said with a Z sound

annotation.walkthrough: Two pronunciations: CLOSE-er with a hard S means nearer, while a CLOZE-er is what ends something, like the last song in a set.
annotation.definitionFit: Closer means nearer, and a closer is the final item or act.
